"Solar, lunar, planetary and sky-chart positions are calculated locally using low-precision approximations, without third-party astronomy services. Terrain obstruction, atmospheric changes and orbital perturbations are not fully modeled. Do not use these results for surveying or navigation.\n\nBuilt-in stellar and deep-sky coordinates and apparent magnitudes are approximate references. A deep-sky object\'s integrated apparent magnitude does not directly indicate naked-eye visibility."

"Wolfx is an unofficial relay service. This app uses only its recent China Earthquake Networks catalog, containing up to about 50 records. It does not provide a global catalog or earthquake early warnings.

Authorization for public redistribution of China Earthquake Networks data through this service has not been fully confirmed. This app has not obtained redistribution permission from China Earthquake Networks. CORS support, technical access, noncommercial use, attribution and disclaimers do not replace permission.

When enabled, the app requests the catalog from Wolfx, which may receive your IP address. Requests exclude reference coordinates. The interface does not guarantee complete coverage, all events or a fixed update delay.

If an official agency or rights holder requests discontinuation, the maintainer will immediately stop the integration, remove the affected installation packages under their control and cooperate with further action. You can disable this source at any time."

"This feature browses recent earthquake catalogs; it does not provide early warnings, wave-arrival countdowns or background earthquake notifications. Events may be missing, publication timing varies, and parameters may be revised. An empty list does not mean no earthquakes occurred. Filters do not imply complete source coverage."

"). Dates include the year; time zones using daylight saving show the offset applicable on the event date. The relayed China Earthquake Networks Center catalog is parsed as UTC+08:00 before conversion. Distances are surface great-circle distances from the reference position to the epicenter, not distances to the hypocenter."

"Sources: GEOFON at the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ / GEVN) and the European–Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC / SeismicPortal), attributed under CC BY 4.0.

Event locations were obtained from the GEOFON program of the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences using data from the GEVN partner networks.

The supplementary U.S. Geological Survey global catalog uses only National Earthquake Information Center solutions (net=us). Third-party images are not copied, and the entire aggregated catalog is not treated as public domain.

The app matches and filters events, formats times and translates some region names. Merged events retain each source's parameters without averaging magnitudes; sources may not be independent. Lists identify contributors; details retain aggregators and relay information. Reviewed Chinese reports take priority, followed by other reviewed reports, then automatic or unknown reports. Newer reports win equal priorities. A Chinese source alone does not imply review."

"Intensity first uses U.S. Geological Survey aggregated felt reports (cdi), labeled source-reported intensity. They are not official field-survey results. ShakeMap mmi values are model results and remain labeled estimated intensity.\n\nLocal estimates represent epicentral reference intensity, not maximum intensity or intensity at the reference location. Valid source updates are adopted automatically. Reviewed models remain models rather than measurements. Only Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) is used; the list omits scale and model parentheses, while details retain the full explanation."

"If no usable source intensity is available, events meeting conditions including Mw 5.0–7.9 and depth greater than 0 and no more than 30 km use Allen, Wald and Worden (2012). Other records with valid magnitude and depth use the PGA and MMI threshold reference algorithm from an older open-source GlobalQuake release.\n\nThe latter accepts magnitudes −2–10.5 and depths 0–800 km. These are accepted input ranges, not guarantees of global applicability or accuracy. Small, deep and tectonically different events may have substantial errors. Results from the two models should not be compared as precisely equivalent calibrations."

"The GlobalQuake reference algorithm is adapted from its older MIT-licensed version, not the current closed-source version. Source magnitude types are retained; non-Mw inputs are marked as approximated using the source magnitude. Details flag 10 km depths and depths marked as default or fixed; these may be catalog defaults rather than reliable measurements. Missing depths are not imputed; values below the first model threshold are not labeled MMI 0. Site effects, rupture geometry and tectonic applicability have not been checked event by event. Estimates are for reference, not disaster-response decisions."
"The scale and model of Wolfx\'s intensity field remain unverified. The app does not use it or treat it as an official maximum intensity."
"German, European and US sources provide supplementary global catalogs."
"\n\nThe German and European sources\' CC BY 4.0 licenses do not apply to China Earthquake Networks Center or Wolfx data."

"Earthquake queries send the selected providers an IP address, client identifier, time range and minimum magnitude. The page refreshes in the foreground at the configured interval, 15 minutes by default. With automatic refresh disabled, even an empty cache does not trigger a request. Manual refreshes are at least one minute apart and follow source rate limits.\n\nCatalog and intensity fields are cached locally, retaining the previous result on failure. Clearing caches preserves settings and rate-limit records. Disabling a source stops its requests and hides its cached records."
"GlobalQuake · Reference algorithm and older MIT release"

"Magnitude measures earthquake size, calculated from wave amplitudes, seismic moment or other quantities. Mw is moment magnitude, ML local magnitude, mb body-wave magnitude and Ms surface-wave magnitude. Different types should not be compared directly. M alone means the source did not specify a type. Magnitudes may be negative; this app\'s lowest filter is M≥0.0."

"Intensity describes shaking effects at a location. One earthquake can have different intensities at different places. This app uses Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI), I–XII, describing felt shaking and effects rather than earthquake size. All listed intensity values use MMI; sources, models and assumptions are given in details."

"Maximum intensity is the highest intensity within a survey or model area. Epicentral intensity applies near the epicenter; they need not be equal. This app estimates epicentral MMI, not intensity at your reference location or an official maximum. Felt aggregates come from questionnaires; model intensities come from calculations. Both can be revised."

"The focus is where underground rupture begins; the epicenter is its corresponding surface location. Depth measures how far the focus is below the surface. Displayed distances run along the surface from your reference location to the epicenter, not in a straight line to the underground focus."

"Natural earthquakes can relate to fault motion, volcanic activity or collapse. Induced earthquakes and nonnatural events such as explosions or nuclear tests also occur. Only source-designated earthquake records or corresponding earthquake types are displayed. Causes are not inferred from location, and quarry blasts are excluded."

"Automatic result: the source marks an automatic solution calculated by its computer system from observations. This marker contains no explicit manual processing or review information; it does not establish whether anyone has looked at it."

"Reviewed: for concise display, this app groups source markers manual, reviewed and confirmed together. Manual means human participation and does not guarantee completion of a formal review procedure. Original markers remain in details."
"Unknown status: no recognizable processing or review marker was provided. It must not be assumed to be automatic."

"Review status restates source markers. It is neither independent verification by this app nor a reliability rating. Parameters of any status can be revised. Review does not turn model intensity into a measurement."

"Location fix uses the last valid position. Refresh location on the earthquake page requests a new fix with the method set in Status. For a manual reference, enter longitude, then latitude, and save. Positive longitude is east E and negative west W; positive latitude is north N and negative south S. Coordinates are used locally for distances and nearby filters, never sent to catalog sources."

"GFZ GEOFON, EMSC and USGS are enabled by default. Wolfx is disabled until you confirm its usage notice. Wolfx provides only a recent Chinese catalog; other sources supplement global coverage. Events merge only on clear matches. Each source\'s parameters remain in details."

"Device heading follows the top edge of the screen. Hold the device flat, away from magnets, metal and electrical equipment. If needed, move it slowly in a figure eight to calibrate. True north requires magnetic declination estimated from a recent location. Pitch is positive with the top edge raised; roll is negative left and positive right."
"Direction of travel comes from location data, not device orientation."

"With rotation disabled, the sky plot has north up, south down, west left and east right. When enabled, it rotates with device heading. The edge is altitude 0° and the center 90°. Azimuth increases clockwise from true north at 0°. Colors identify systems; filled markers contribute to the current fix, hollow markers do not. Tap a satellite for details."

"Only satellites reported by the device chipset and Android are shown, not a calculated complete constellation. Precise location permission is required. Starting reception also starts position updates using the Status location method. Stopping reception leaves location running; stopping location also stops reception. Reception and continuous location each follow their own lifecycle settings. Assisted positioning may use a network; this app downloads no ephemerides."
"Precise location permission is required to read satellite status"
"The selected satellite is no longer reported or is hidden"

"Places use their chosen colors; a ring marks the target and the center is your current position. The target distance determines the outer range; without a target, the farthest visible place sets it. Out-of-range places appear as smaller points on the edge. Set colors and visibility in place management; tap a point to target it. With valid heading and location, the plot rotates with the device; otherwise true north is up. Distances are great-circle surface distances and bearings are initial bearings, without roads or obstacles. Location and magnetic errors affect results; do not use for safety navigation. Places are stored locally and support app JSON import/export. Clearing cache or resetting settings preserves them; uninstalling deletes them."

"Drag with one finger to pan and use the slider to zoom. The square spans 30 meters at the left endpoint and 10 kilometers at the right. Edge scales follow zoom; zoom is centered on the frame. Pinch zoom is disabled. Tap a point for its index, coordinates and time.

Selecting a saved route first shows its full preview. Playback reveals points from the start. Follow position tracks the orange playback point or your device during recording; tap again or pan to stop following. When paused, step between points or jump to either end, centering the chosen point.

Recording defaults to every 5 seconds, adjustable to 2–60 seconds in Status settings. With network location, recording cannot be faster than the network interval. Enable continuous location and start location before recording. Missing valid fixes pauses recording; new fixes resume it. Routes are stored locally and support app JSON import/export."
"Enable continuous location in Status settings and start location first"
"Finish the current recording before viewing saved routes"

"The app requests sensor data at the highest available rate and targets a 50 ms display interval. Actual frequency depends on hardware and system scheduling; the last reading is retained until new data arrives. Sensors absent or inaccessible to the system are shown as unavailable.

Sensor axes are fixed to the device's natural orientation: X points right, Y points up, and Z points outward from the screen. The gyroscope reports angular velocity rather than rotation angle. The accelerometer includes gravity and supports motion and tilt detection; linear acceleration attempts to remove gravity; the gravity sensor estimates gravitational acceleration for orientation reference.

Battery temperature in the Battery section describes the battery itself and differs from ambient temperature. The system ambient-light sensor reports illuminance."
"All battery information is hidden in settings."

"Health status is reported by Android. It does not measure remaining capacity or guarantee safety. Current polarity can be changed in Status settings; manufacturers use different conventions. Missing data are not shown as zero."
"All device information is hidden in settings."

"Compass, system sensor and battery data are read while Status is in the foreground. Camera sampling follows its separate setting. Started satellite reception pauses on tab changes, screen lock or backgrounding and resumes on return by default. If automatic resume is disabled, reception must be started manually.

To continue positioning outside Status, enable continuous location in Settings → Status, then start location manually. Stop from the notification or Status. If notifications are denied, use the system's active-app controls. Battery restrictions, permission changes or force stop may interrupt location.

Android supplies horizontal and vertical uncertainties, typically at approximately 68% confidence; they do not guarantee a maximum error. Vertical uncertainty describes altitude uncertainty. Missing values show Vertical accuracy not provided. Altitude is WGS84 ellipsoid height, not height above mean sea level. Altitude not provided does not mean zero.

Satellite hardware positioning uses supported satellite signals and needs no app network connection. Indoor use or obstructions can prevent fixes. System-assisted positioning may use a network.

Network positioning requires a system network-location service and connectivity. The system may send IP, cell-tower or Wi-Fi information to its provider under that provider's rules. Devices without such a service cannot use it. The interval is the shortest requested update interval; updates may be delayed or reuse earlier results.

Coordinates use WGS84, longitude then latitude: E east, W west, N north and S south. This app does not upload location coordinates. Earthquake distances and place bearings are calculated locally. Fix age uses the location result's actual timestamp."

"1.2.9 · Colors, sky pointing and ambient light"

"• Added global colors for primary, explanatory and accent text, plus button backgrounds and labels, with presets and custom #RRGGBB values. Invalid historical colors fall back to blue.
• Sky pointing uses rotation-vector sensors and a red crosshair, with rear-camera or top-edge reference.
• Camera brightness sampling runs without a preview or manual start; background continuation is optional and off by default.
• Reorganized sensor notes, settings and paragraphs; distinguished battery and ambient temperature and removed redundant weather and sky text.
• Normalized Chinese place names and aliases, including Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, to avoid duplicate local and online results.
• Version 1.2.9 / versionCode 33."
"1.2.8 · Region deduplication, export and device tools"

"• Removed preset city buttons; retained saved regions and search. Deduplicated normalized names and coordinates, with an offline Chinese city catalog covering mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan and retaining GeoNames attribution and coordinate checks.
• Added saved-route renaming and ordering, plus global configuration export for settings, favorite regions, places, routes and timetable JSON.
• Added rotation-vector sky pointing, with fixed horizontal coordinates when unavailable.
• Ambient light can use the system sensor or front/rear camera. Camera readings are relative image brightness, not calibrated illuminance.
• Version 1.2.8 / versionCode 32."

"• New UI text uses XML resources. Added a global language entry; Chinese remains the complete language pending formal switching in 2.0.0.
• Removed common-region buttons; expanded normalized Chinese city names across mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, including Suqian and Suzhou districts, with deduplication.
• Saved places support ordering; editing preserves list position.
• Added maximum-UV-index notes below weather details.
• Version 1.2.7 / versionCode 31."

"• Import/export saved places and routes as JSON through the system picker. Imports require confirmation, keep existing records and skip duplicates.
• Compass defaults to true north, with default choices first. Removed north-reference parentheses from travel direction.
• Fixed zoom changing when replay restarts at the end.
• Added route edge scales and a 30 m–10 km zoom range.
• Follow-position toggles and follows the orange playback point.
• Place-diagram range follows the selected target; distant places appear smaller on the edge.
• Version 1.2.6; original signing key retained."

"• Refined terminology, prompts and long-note paragraph spacing.
• Centered replay follows the orange point continuously; dragging cancels following.
• Combined start/stop controls for location and satellite reception. Reception also starts location so route recording works.
• Vertical uncertainty appears below altitude in large text.
• Places support colors, visibility and multiple plotted targets.
• Overlapping-point details use Back and retain the point-selection list.
• Version 1.2.5; original signing key retained."

"• Preserve scroll position when satellite details and status values update.
• Zoom around the route-frame center, including after panning.
• Status displays other than GPS location target 50 ms updates; actual data depend on the system. GPS and network intervals retain their settings.
• Confirm deletion of saved or unsaved routes; cancellation keeps the route.
• Default order: Compass, Current location, Satellites, Places, Route recording, Sensors, Battery, Device and environment, Usage notes; customized order retained.
• Version 1.2.4 / versionCode 26; compatible signed upgrade."

"• Added route recording with continuous location at 2–60 second intervals, zoom slider, panning, centering and point details; finish to name/save or delete and replay.
• Enlarged pitch/roll, clarified network interval names and disabled long-press selection in ordinary notes.
• Refined place-refresh and direction notes. Added global background, outline and time settings shared across pages.
• Version 1.2.3 / versionCode 25, upgradable over 1.2.2.
• Maintenance combined recording controls and removed pan mode and pinch zoom; added full-route preview, incremental play/pause, paused stepping and endpoint jumps, 1–20 points/s speed and name-field padding."

"• Repositioned heavy-thunderstorm hail to avoid an outward-launch appearance.
• Moved location-setting links to the end of usage notes; ordered Status settings and added battery/device visibility and order.
• Battery current can retain system polarity or reverse it; default matches 1.2.0, with manufacturer-convention notes.
• Satellite names use country/region plus abbreviation. Reception pauses outside Status and resumes on return; removed sensor frame-rate settings.
• Place forms show live fix age and refresh coordinates only on request; removed the app-level place limit.
• Cache management shows storage usage; reordered settings."

"• Added sensor visibility/order, rotating satellite plots, satellite sorting by system or carrier-to-noise density, and battery/gravity explanations.
• Corrected pitch/roll conventions, displayed local declination and enlarged ground speed and travel direction.
• Satellite reception pauses across tabs, screen lock and background by default, with a stop option. No app-level place limit.
• Version 1.2.1 / versionCode 23, upgradable over 1.2.0."

"• Location became Status, retaining methods, intervals, foreground service and shared last fix.
• Added a 16-point compass, true/magnetic north, pitch/roll and calibration notes with display-rotation compensation.
• Added device-reported GPS, BeiDou, Galileo, GLONASS and other satellite plots, angles, signal density and fix contribution; precise permission and compatible hardware required. Reception stopped outside the page.
• Added local saved places, manual/current coordinates, target point, distance and bearing, without road maps or routes.
• Added available gyroscope, acceleration, gravity, magnetic, pressure and light sensors, plus battery, current, memory, storage and uptime.
• Status sections support visibility/order and satellite filtering; processing remains local without third-party status services or code."
"1.1.6 · Tablet state restoration and more sky objects"

"• Fixed acquired earthquake status becoming cached and loss of tab/time state on tablet rotation or resizing.
• Added northern bright stars and brighter clusters, nebulae and galaxies with approximate integrated magnitudes and M-number-first names. Included all seven main Orion stars, retained old visibility/selection identities and made all Big Dipper stars selectable.
• Added manual or magnitude-threshold display in 0.1 steps while preserving manual choices.
• Clarified negative/positive longitude as west/east and latitude as south/north."

"• Requested portrait pages to avoid rotation-driven reconstruction and state changes.\n• Prioritized reviewed Chinese reports, then other reviewed reports, then automatic or unknown reports; newer equal-priority reports win, with no extra German-source preference.\n• Lists show concrete contributors such as Chilean and Thai agencies, with deduplication and aggregator/relay details retained."

"• Simplified statuses to Reviewed, Automatic result and Unknown, retaining original markers in details.
• Clarified event time and simplified list intensity/source labels, with model/relay detail and below-threshold messages retained.
• Kept only MMI; removed other scale settings and unhelpful unspecified fixed-depth notes.
• Translated contributors, standardized longitude-before-latitude with hemisphere letters, and clarified earliest-record status."
"1.1.3 · Earthquake UI and wider intensity reference"

"• Filters retain catalog/location refresh only; other controls move to settings. Standardized Last 1 day and removed a duplicate privacy link.
• Standardized paragraph spacing; put MMI first and migrated the scale once while preserving later choices.
• Outside conservative paper conditions, use an older MIT-licensed GlobalQuake reference algorithm with valid magnitude/depth, noting approximations, fixed depths and weak-shaking thresholds; not official maximum intensity.
• Clarified automatic solutions and review/manual terminology; removed mainshock/foreshock/aftershock notes."

"• Added a 0–7 magnitude slider, step 0.1, default M≥1.0, nearby radius 50–5000 km and location/manual reference choices with automatic distance updates.
• Added one-shot fixes on the earthquake page, coordinates, full-year dates, clearer sorting and consolidated time/source/privacy notes; added terminology.
• Added USGS global supplementation and unambiguous event merging. Agency names are translated. Wolfx is off by default until confirmed, with takedown cooperation stated.
• Distinguished felt reports, source models and local MMI estimates; no unverified Chinese-scale conversion or extrapolation outside the original model range."

"• Integrated up to 50 recent CENC records via Wolfx, with separate cache, refresh and source toggle. Merge with GEOFON/EMSC only on clear matches, retaining parameters.\n• Explicitly stated that public redistribution authorization remains unconfirmed. CORS and noncommercial use are not permission; the source can be disabled.\n• Parse event/report times as Beijing time. No completeness or period-coverage guarantee; unverified intensity fields and early-warning streams are excluded."

"• Added GEOFON/EMSC recent catalogs, nearby-event merging, magnitude types, times, depth, epicenter, surface distance and source details.
• Added time/area/magnitude/radius/sort/time-zone/intensity/field/order/foreground-refresh settings and per-source cached status.
• Retained CC BY 4.0 attribution; Wolfx remained disabled pending upstream authorization. No warning stream or unsupported intensity values.
• Added optional continuous foreground-service location, off by default, with a persistent stop notification. Last fix is used locally for earthquake distance.
• Cache management includes earthquake catalogs and blocks stale in-flight responses after clearing. Existing tab order and settings remain."

"• Settings appear directly at center without slide animations. Spacing/outlines are prepared before layout; date input follows the same behavior, with hierarchical back navigation and validation.\n• Renamed browser action to Open in browser, matching map buttons in size, radius and spacing, with small-screen wrapping.\n• Researched earthquake sources and licenses without adding the feature."

"• Standardized navigation, sorting, time, timetable, crop and dialog spacing. Removed duplicate region-picker triggers and moved Search outside the input.
• Added Moscow and Paris to common regions; adjusted crop wording and renamed Term settings.
• Collapsed version entries by default on every visit. Added cache management preserving long-term data and rate limits.
• Added astronomy time controls and section visibility/order, preserving selection and scroll.
• Week jumping uses direct input; reduced icon size for white margins. Earthquakes remained research only."

"• Enlarged the square local-sky chart. Labels stay above/below points, hiding on conflicts while retaining selection.
• Renamed selected-object information. Sun and Moon are selectable; Moon magnitude is locally estimated and Sun magnitude omitted.
• Added separate Moon phase, illumination, approximate age, time to full Moon and a changing phase diagram.
• Added the official NMC weather-chart page after satellite imagery.
• Put default course-prefix options first, preserving selections."

"• Simplified WMO legend notes and unknown-weather explanations.
• Refined default wording, full course prefixes and 5-second location interval.
• Added planet/deep-sky visibility and horizontal, polar equatorial and grid-free modes.
• Selected objects use a slowly rotating broken crosshair, retained through time changes and hidden below the horizon.
• Standardized Vega, Altair and Polaris Chinese names, preserving preferences; added Pleiades and Andromeda centers from CC0 coordinates.

"Weather data is provided by Open-Meteo and location search is based on GeoNames, with CC BY 4.0 attribution. The app formats descriptions, rounding and units for display.

Current weather is a numerical-model estimate, not an on-site station observation or a replacement for official warnings. Current and hourly timestamps follow the time-display setting; daily forecasts and sunrise and sunset retain the selected location's time zone.

No account, advertisements, analytics or app-operated server is used. Weather and location searches require network access; providers may receive IP addresses, search terms and selected location coordinates. The free Open-Meteo API is limited to noncommercial use; commercial use requires separate authorization. Weather is cached for 15 minutes, manual requests are at least one minute apart, and rate limits pause requests.

Precipitation, temperature, radar, satellite and weather charts are viewed on official pages within the app. Copyright belongs to the National Meteorological Centre and other original rights holders, and those sites process visits under their own policies. Astronomy results are approximated locally."

"Timetables, backgrounds, favorites, places, routes, random selection lists and draw records, and the most recent location are stored on this device. Earthquake distances, place bearings and configuration imports are processed locally; these data are not uploaded. Clearing cache or restoring defaults retains saved places, routes, random selection lists and progress, and the selected target. Uninstalling the app deletes local data.

Status uses Android system APIs for orientation, sensors, battery and satellite reception. Satellite status requires precise location permission. Reception away from the Status tab follows your settings. Continuous location must be enabled explicitly and runs as a foreground service. System network and assisted location may send IP, cell tower or Wi-Fi information to service providers under their own policies. The app does not connect to third-party ephemeris services or read device serial numbers, IMEI or MAC addresses.

Camera ambient-light sampling requires camera permission and processes brightness samples only in memory, without saving or uploading images. You can pause sampling to close the camera. Sampling stops by default when leaving Status; allowing background sampling remains subject to system restrictions.

JSON files you choose to export may contain coordinates, timestamps, names and other personal settings. Place files also contain colors and visibility. You choose the destination through the system file picker; cloud providers and other file providers apply their own privacy policies. Compass bearings, place directions and route diagrams are affected by sensors, magnetic fields, location and model errors, and are not intended for professional surveying or safety navigation."

"Left icons represent daytime and right icons nighttime. The rightmost value is the WMO weather code. WMO code numbers belong to the meteorological code table; weather_code is the API field.

Open-Meteo documents only a subset of WMO codes. Icons cover these codes, so gaps in numbering are expected.

Names follow the WMO English table. Codes 57 and 67 mean moderate or heavy freezing drizzle and freezing rain. Thunderstorm codes include 95, 96, 97 and 99. Forecast codes may be model-derived rather than original observation codes.

Slight or moderate thunderstorms with hail and heavy thunderstorms with hail are returned only by models providing the relevant hail forecasts, such as DWD ICON and UKMO, depending on coverage and model capabilities."
